name: AgenTracer: Who Is Inducing Failure in the LLM Agentic Systems?
authors: Guibin Zhang, Junhao Wang, Junjie Chen (equal contribution), Wangchunshu Zhou, Kun Wang, Shuicheng Yan. Lead affiliation: National University of Singapore (NUS); also CUHK, OPPO, NTU.
venue: arXiv preprint (2025); also under review (OpenReview submission, id l05DseqvuD)
feedback_source: external-tool/oracle during data construction (counterfactual replay uses an oracle rectification operator with ground-truth solution G and environmental feedback F; programmatic fault injection uses an attacker/perturbation operator); the deployed AgenTracer-8B tracer itself acts as a learned retrospective critic that emits attribution + reasoning feedback to the failing multi-agent system.
iteration_structure: Data construction: episodic counterfactual replay (sequential per-step oracle rectification with re-simulation until the earliest decisive error is found) plus single-shot programmatic fault injection. Deployment for self-improvement: episodic-retry, iterated for 3 rounds where the tracer's feedback is injected into the next problem-solving episode.
reflection_object: action trajectory / agent-level credit assignment: AgenTracer reflects on a full multi-agent execution trajectory (logs + environmental feedback) and localizes the decisive error step and the failure-responsible agent; the learning that produces the tracer modifies model weights (QWEN3-8B fine-tuned via RL). The feedback delivered downstream targets the failing agent's action/reasoning for the next episode.
requires_training: RL (online GRPO-style policy optimization with dynamic clipping on QWEN3-8B); the curated TracerTraj-2.5K dataset is built by an oracle-driven annotation pipeline rather than human SFT labels.
reward_or_critic_model: verifiable reward / separate retrospective model. Training uses a programmatic multi-granular reward (binary agent-level indicator + Gaussian step-level proximity reward, gated by a strict binary format reward); the resulting AgenTracer-8B is itself a separate trained failure-tracer (retrospective critic) for downstream multi-agent systems.
distillation_target: model-weights: the oracle-annotated failure-attribution knowledge (TracerTraj-2.5K) is distilled into the weights of the lightweight AgenTracer-8B tracer via RL.
emergent_vs_engineered: engineered: the failure-attribution capability is explicitly trained via a designed multi-granular RL reward over an automatically-annotated dataset, not RL-emergent self-reflection. The tracer does emit a <think>...</think> reasoning trace, but the attribution behavior is deliberately optimized rather than spontaneously emergent.
memory_type: none (no persistent memory store for the tracer); it operates over the full provided trajectory log in an 'all-at-once' single-pass setting. The reusable artifact is the released TracerTraj-2.5K dataset, not a runtime memory.
memory_persistence: within-episode (the tracer consumes a single trajectory per inference; in the self-improvement loop, feedback is passed cross-episode within the same task across 3 rounds).
memory_curation_mechanism: n/a (no runtime memory curation; for the training dataset, curation is done by counterfactual-replay annotation selecting the earliest decisive error and a 9:1 train/test split).
error_localization_granularity: step-level and agent-level (multi-agent): AgenTracer outputs both the decisive error step t* and the failure-responsible agent i*, supervised by a multi-granular reward at both granularities.
intra_task_vs_inter_task: inter-task: the tracer is trained on trajectories from six frameworks and six datasets and generalizes to unseen Who&When trajectories; the diagnostic feedback transfers experience across episodes/tasks to improve downstream systems.
failure_recovery_vs_avoidance: avoidance-only / post-hoc-revision: AgenTracer performs post-hoc failure attribution on a completed failed trajectory, then supplies feedback used to avoid the error in subsequent retry rounds (it does not correct mid-trajectory in-flight).
task_domains: code, math (mathematical reasoning), general agentic tasks (tool-use / QA / decision-making); applied to multi-agent system debugging and self-evolution.
benchmarks: Who&When (handcraft subset from Magnetic-One and automated subset from AG2); TracerTraj-Code, TracerTraj-Math, TracerTraj-Agentic held-out test sets. Underlying task datasets: MBPP+, KodCode, Blackjack, GAIA, HotpotQA, MATH, GSM8K. Downstream systems boosted: MetaGPT and MaAS (Multi-agent Architecture Search / agentic supernet).
headline_result: AgenTracer-8B outperforms giant proprietary LLMs on Who&When by up to 18.18% (vs Gemini-2.5-Pro) and ~12.21% (vs DeepSeek-R1) in attribution accuracy; on Who&When (handcraft) it reaches 69.10/63.82 agent-level (w/ G / w/o G) and 20.68/20.68 step-level, beating the best baselines (Claude-Sonnet-4 56.90/50.00 agent, 17.24/18.97 step). As actionable feedback it boosts off-the-shelf multi-agent systems (MetaGPT, MaAS) by 4.8-14.2%.
baselines: Attribution baselines: DeepSeek-R1, Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-Sonnet-4, GPT-4.1, Qwen3-32B, Qwen3-Coder, Qwen3-8B (untrained backbone), Llama-3.2-3B. Self-improvement baselines: Self-Refine and CRITIC (both instantiated with GPT-4.1).
gains_vs_baseline: On Who&When vs the strongest comparable reasoning LLMs: +18.18% over Gemini-2.5-Pro and +12.21% over DeepSeek-R1 (headline deltas). Per-table examples: on Who&When (handcraft) agent-level w/ G, AgenTracer 69.10 vs DeepSeek-R1/Claude-Sonnet-4 56.90 (+12.2); on TracerTraj-Math step-level w/o G, AgenTracer 57.63 vs Claude-Sonnet-4 46.03 (+11.6). For downstream self-improvement, AgenTracer-8B feedback yields 4.8-14.2% gains over the failing system and outperforms Self-Refine/CRITIC over 3 iterative rounds.
compute_cost_profile: Tracer is a lightweight 8B model (QWEN3-8B backbone), explicitly positioned as cheaper than calling giant proprietary LLMs (Gemini-2.5-Pro, Claude-Sonnet-4, DeepSeek-R1) for attribution. Inference uses a single 'all-at-once' pass over the trajectory. Training: RL on the verl platform on one server with 8x NVIDIA H100 (80GB), batch size 32, rollout number 8, learning rate 1e-6. Data construction incurs extra cost from oracle counterfactual replay (per-step re-simulation) and DeepSeek-R1-based analyzer/perturbation. Self-improvement adds ~3 extra rollout rounds per task.
known_limitations: Failure attribution is intrinsically hard: errors are subtle, originate early, and stay hidden behind seemingly correct later outputs. Absolute step-level accuracy remains modest on the hardest sets (e.g. ~20.68% on Who&When handcraft step-level). Providing ground truth G does not consistently help and can mislead attribution. The decisive-error formalization assumes a single earliest pivotal error and an oracle rectification operator, which may not capture compound/interacting failures. Reliance on DeepSeek-R1 as analyzer/perturbation for data generation introduces dependence on a strong external model.
oracle_or_external_feedback_dependency: Training data construction is oracle-dependent (uses ground-truth solution G + environmental feedback F + oracle rectification for counterfactual replay, and known-by-construction labels for fault injection). At deployment, the tracer is evaluated both w/ G (oracle access) and w/o G (no ground truth); the harder, more practical w/o-G setting is emphasized and AgenTracer-8B remains strong there, indicating it does not require oracle labels at inference time.
self_correction_efficacy: net-positive: AgenTracer-8B's feedback delivers consistent 4.8-14.2% downstream gains to MetaGPT/MaAS and beats Self-Refine and CRITIC; attribution remains robust in the w/o-G setting (e.g. maintains 57.63% step-level on TracerTraj-Math while DeepSeek-R1 drops ~9.21% without G), suggesting improvement without label leakage.
calibration_effect: not-measured (the paper does not report confidence calibration of the tracer; it focuses on attribution accuracy and downstream task gains).
failure_attribution_capability: attributes-responsible-agent + attributes-failing-step + counterfactual-localization: AgenTracer identifies both the failure-responsible agent i* and the decisive error step t*, localized via counterfactual replay (oracle rectification with re-simulation to find the earliest step whose correction flips failure to success).
failure_mode_addressed: Targets the general space of multi-agent system failures characterized by MAST (14 failure patterns ranging from task/role disobedience to reasoning-action mismatches) and the high failure rates (up to 86.7%) reported by the UC Berkeley study; specifically localizes the single decisive error (root cause) within long traces, including early hidden errors that propagate (e.g. a Web-Surfer agent retrieving the wrong file early, only revealed many steps later). Relevant MAST-style modes: improper task decomposition, role disobedience, premature/incorrect intermediate results, error propagation across agents.
dataset_or_benchmark_released: Yes: TracerTraj (TracerTraj-2.5K) released - 2,000+ high-fidelity annotated trajectory-error pairs (Coding 1288, Mathematical Reasoning 630, General Agentic 558; curated trajectories 2170/1185/1300 respectively), spanning six multi-agent frameworks (MetaGPT, AutoGen, Smolagents, AgentPrune, AFlow, OWL-Workforce) and benchmarks (MBPP+, KodCode, Blackjack, MATH, GSM8K, GAIA, HotpotQA). Code and model released at https://github.com/bingreeky/AgenTracer.
builds_on: Who&When / 'Which Agent Causes Task Failures and When?' (Zhang et al. 2025, arXiv:2505.00212) for the failure-attribution task formulation and benchmark; MAST 'Why Do Multi-Agent LLM Systems Fail?' (Cemri et al. 2025, arXiv:2503.13657) for failure taxonomy and 'all-at-once' evaluation; QWEN3-8B backbone (Yang et al. 2025); DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al. 2025) as analyzer/perturbation model; verl RL training platform; GRPO-style RL; multi-agent frameworks MetaGPT, AutoGen, Smolagents, AgentPrune, AFlow, OWL-Workforce. Conceptually related to Self-Refine (Madaan et al. 2023) and CRITIC (Gou et al. 2024).
citation_count: 48 (Semantic Scholar, as of June 2026); influential citation count 5
reasoning_model_native: partial: the tracer is trained from a reasoning model (QWEN3-8B) and emits a <think>...</think> reasoning trace used as feedback, and it is evaluated against reasoning-LLM baselines (o1/R1/Gemini-2.5-Pro/Claude-Sonnet-4). It is not specifically designed to require o1/R1-style built-in reflection; rather it demonstrates that small RL-trained tracers beat large reasoning models at attribution.
on_policy_distillation_link: Related but distinct: AgenTracer uses online (on-policy) GRPO-style RL with a programmatic verifiable reward rather than distillation from a teacher model. It can be viewed as distilling oracle-derived counterfactual attribution labels into an 8B policy via RL; no explicit on-policy distillation from a teacher is used.
sample_efficiency: Trained on TracerTraj-2.5K (~2,000+ annotated trajectory-error pairs, 9:1 train/test split) with RL (batch size 32, rollout number 8) on 8x H100; the resulting 8B model outperforms far larger LLMs, indicating strong data/parameter efficiency. Self-improvement loop reaches gains within 3 iterative rounds. Exact gradient-step count not reported.
